subject.label: 2020–2023 container shipping pandemic shock, congestion supercycle, and normalization

cycle_window.note: Orientation window only; exact phase boundaries require post-seal evidence.

subject.why_representative: This cycle should expose multiple interacting shipping variables—spot and contract freight, effective capacity, blank sailings, port congestion, schedule reliability, vessel ordering, inventory/demand normalization, and carrier/shipper expectations—while providing several historical cutoffs where later normalization must not leak backward.

blind_recall_protocol.precision_policy: Preserve approximate dates and uncertain roles instead of fabricating exactness.
blind_recall_protocol.contamination_rule: After seal, search findings may verify, refine, contradict, or split these leads only in new evidence/reconciliation artifacts; they must not rewrite this blind packet.

cycle_phase_leads.memory_lead: Initial COVID shock appears to have produced expectations of severe trade-demand weakness; liner carriers responded with capacity withdrawals/blank sailings and network adjustments.
unknowns: Exact timing and scale by trade lane
Which carrier/alliance announcements best capture contemporaneous expectations
How quickly spot-rate weakness versus capacity discipline diverged by route

cycle_phase_leads.memory_lead: Goods demand, equipment imbalance, port/terminal congestion and inland logistics constraints appear to have tightened effective container shipping capacity and driven exceptional freight-rate increases.
unknowns: Relative contribution of demand, congestion, equipment scarcity and carrier capacity management
Which bottlenecks were globally binding versus lane-specific
When participants first expected normalization and how those dates moved

cycle_phase_leads.memory_lead: A central contemporaneous debate appears to have been whether elevated carrier earnings and rates were a temporary congestion windfall or a more durable shift supported by consolidation, contracts, capacity discipline and logistics integration.
unknowns: Carrier-specific language distinguishing temporary versus structural earnings
Shipper and freight-forwarder expectations for contract-rate resets
Whether alliance/consolidation claims were explicit causal judgments or later interpretations

cycle_phase_leads.memory_lead: Large containership newbuild ordering appears to have raised a forward oversupply question: once congestion unwound and new tonnage delivered, effective capacity could rise faster than demand.
unknowns: Orderbook-to-fleet ratios at each historical cutoff
Delivery schedule by size class and fuel specification
How much slow steaming, scrapping or environmental rules were expected to offset deliveries

cycle_phase_leads.memory_lead: As goods demand and congestion eased, market expectations appear to have shifted toward normalization of spot freight, schedule reliability and carrier profitability, with uncertainty around how fast contract rates and capacity deployment would follow.
unknowns: Exact sequence of spot-rate decline, congestion relief and contract repricing
Carrier guidance revisions during the normalization
Which later outcomes were already knowable at each cutoff

metric_leads.memory_use: spot container freight-rate signal on selected export trades
metric_leads.precision_risk: route composition and units must be verified

metric_leads.metric: Drewry World Container Index and/or Freightos Baltic Index
metric_leads.precision_risk: methodology, route basket and contract basis must not be conflated

metric_leads.metric: Carrier average freight rate / revenue per TEU
metric_leads.precision_risk: definitions differ by carrier and period
accounting definitions and business mix differ
announced versus realized capacity must be separated

metric_leads.metric: Idle fleet / active fleet / effective capacity
metric_leads.precision_risk: nominal slots are not the same as effective capacity under congestion

metric_leads.metric: Port dwell time / vessel waiting / congestion indicators

metric_leads.precision_risk: provider methodology and schedule definitions require verification
TEU versus vessel count, delivery timing, cancellations and size-class mix matter
actual operating speed and regulatory effects need evidence

metric_leads.metric: Long-term contract freight rates / renewal levels
metric_leads.memory_use: lagged shipper-carrier expectations and earnings persistence
metric_leads.precision_risk: private contracts and benchmark proxies may differ

judgment_leads.memory_judgment: Participants likely feared a sharp trade collapse and prioritized capacity withdrawal over expansion.
judgment_leads.later_outcome_must_remain_separate: Do not use later freight-rate strength to rewrite the contemporaneous demand fear.

judgment_leads.memory_judgment: Repeated expectations may have called for congestion/rates to normalize after successive near-term milestones, only for bottlenecks to persist.
judgment_leads.later_outcome_must_remain_separate: Each forecast date and revision must be reconstructed from what was knowable then.

judgment_leads.memory_judgment: Carriers and investors debated temporary congestion rents versus structurally improved liner economics after consolidation, alliances and contract repricing.
judgment_leads.later_outcome_must_remain_separate: Do not infer the original rationale from 2023 normalization.

judgment_leads.memory_judgment: The rapidly growing newbuild orderbook likely became a key bearish medium-term supply argument, conditional on congestion easing and deliveries arriving on schedule.
judgment_leads.later_outcome_must_remain_separate: The later rate decline cannot by itself prove what participants expected or why.

judgment_leads.memory_judgment: A normalization thesis likely combined easing goods demand, inventory correction, less port congestion and future vessel deliveries, but timing remained uncertain.
judgment_leads.later_outcome_must_remain_separate: Separate the forecast components from the actual pace of normalization.

explicit_unknowns: Exact historical rate levels, peaks, troughs and dates for each benchmark
Exact port congestion/waiting metrics and when each source first published them
Carrier-by-carrier guidance, quotes and revision chronology
Which shippers/forwarders publicly documented allocation scarcity, contract resets or expected normalization
Orderbook magnitude and expected delivery schedule at each historical cutoff
How IMO efficiency/carbon rules were expected to affect effective capacity versus how they later did
Whether equipment shortage was an independent bottleneck or mostly a symptom of network congestion in each phase
How much rate strength came from demand versus capacity discipline versus congestion; no causal share is accepted from memory
Which alliance actions were operational responses versus evidence of durable market power
The exact knowledge-time boundary for each later normalization signal
post_seal_search_families: Carrier annual/interim reports, earnings calls, guidance and investor materials
Port authority/terminal throughput and congestion releases
Index-provider methodology and historical freight-rate series
UNCTAD/industry statistical publications with publication dates preserved
Shipper/forwarder public statements and contract-market benchmarks
Reverse queries for high-impact claims that appear resolved

evidence_acceptance_boundary.publication_rule: No Fact, Reality or Judgment is publishable from this packet alone.
evidence_acceptance_boundary.claim_scope_rule: Evidence authority must be evaluated for the exact claim, not by source prestige alone.
evidence_acceptance_boundary.source_state_rule: Distinguish locator_verified, content_verified and materialized; a locator alone cannot prove a claim.
evidence_acceptance_boundary.content_rule: Claim-relevant content must actually be read and anchored to page/section/excerpt or faithful readable representation.
evidence_acceptance_boundary.conflict_rule: Conflicting authoritative sources remain explicit; do not majority-vote or silently reconcile.

pit_acceptance_boundary.known_time_rule: A historical cutoff may include only information conservatively knowable by that cutoff.
pit_acceptance_boundary.precision_rule: Keep source-supported temporal precision; do not invent exact dates for approximate memory.
pit_acceptance_boundary.revision_rule: Later guidance/outcomes append as new versions and never overwrite earlier judgments.
pit_acceptance_boundary.acceptance_question: At each cutoff, what could a rational shipping participant know and reasonably believe, and what remained unresolved?

seal.seal_reason: Initial actor, metric, phase, contemporaneous-judgment and unknown-space coverage is sufficient to start post-seal claim-scoped verification without further blind-memory expansion.
seal.next_allowed_step: Create post-seal claim-scoped evidence tasks; do not mutate this packet with search-derived facts.
